items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: Henry Mancini’s book, which really took the complete mystery out of it because I couldn’t imagine how those sounds were made

ctx.x: Henry Mancini’s book, which really took the complete mystery out of it because I couldn’t imagine how those sounds were made but his book had the piano part and then a CD that had the “now you put it with these strings” “now you put it with four horns and here’s how it sounds.” Ah. And so, and of course I had the best players in the world. I

mean when I wrote, the first time I wrote a string chart — the first time I wrote a string chart the string players went [scats]. They said, “Anne, you have to put the slur over.” So that’s how much I knew. But I could, you know, get the ranges of all the instruments and one of the arrangers said, “Just don’t do anything to show off how difficult you can write.”
